    <h1>Solar neutrinos</h1>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
Nuclear reactions in the Sun produce electron neutrinos $\nu_e$. Measurements of the solar neutrino flux proved that nuclear reactions take place in the Sun. The deficit of the measured flux $\Phi(E)_{\nu_e}$ was explained by Mikheyev, Smirnov and Wolfenstein as a result of neutrino oscillations in the matter of the Sun. This made it possible to measure the mixing angle $\theta_{12}$ and the difference of the squared neutrino masses $\Delta m^2_{21}\equiv m_2^2-m_1^2$.

\(i\) Compute the cross sections of the reactions $\nu_e + e^- \to e^- + \nu_e$ ($W$ and $Z$ exchange) and $\nu_\mu + e^- \to \nu_\mu + e^-$ ($Z$ exchange). Plot them as functions of the neutrino energy for $E_\nu\in(1,10)$ MeV.

\(ii\) In the Super-Kamiokande experiment (Japan), solar neutrino interactions are observed by detecting the Cherenkov light of the recoil electrons. In a model with two neutrino types, $\nu_e$ and $\nu_\mu$, neutrino oscillations redistribute the fluxes, $\Phi_{\nu_e}\leftrightarrow\Phi_{\nu_\mu}$. How did physicists conclude that there is a deficit of recoil electrons, if electrons appear in both reactions, $\nu_e + e^- \to e^- + \nu_e$ and $\nu_\mu + e^- \to \nu_\mu + e^-$? Support your answer with numerical estimates.

\(iii\) Compute the expected number of recoil-electron events per year in a water detector of mass 50 kt, assuming a solar neutrino flux $\Phi=5.7\cdot 10^{6}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ and a mean energy $\langle E_\nu\rangle =8.5$ MeV.

\(iv\) The electron neutrino $|\nu_e\rangle = \cos\theta|\nu_1\rangle+\sin\theta|\nu_2\rangle$ and the muon neutrino $|\nu_\mu\rangle = -\sin\theta|\nu_1\rangle+\cos\theta|\nu_2\rangle$ are coherent superpositions of the mass states $|\nu_{1,2}\rangle$. Because of the Mikheyev--Smirnov--Wolfenstein effect, for energies $E_\nu\ge 5$ MeV what leaves the Sun is neither $|\nu_e\rangle$ nor $|\nu_\mu\rangle$ but the pure mass state $|\nu_2\rangle$. Revisit items (i), (ii), (iii) in the light of this fact and discuss your conclusions.

:::
